label: GTX 1080 Three-Pose Walking Cycle
notes: Prefer a complete eight-phase gait: contact, down, passing, up, then the opposite-leg contact, down, passing, and up.
Three-pose input remains a preview fallback and is not considered biomechanically complete.
Use transparent character poses and composite them onto one approved environment plate before interpolation.
Keep identity, camera, props, character scale, and lighting fixed across poses.
Use clean key-pose holds for generated sprites; enable RIFE only when adjacent poses have rig-consistent limbs and pass a 24-frame deformation review.
Normalize every sprite by its alpha bounds, anchor its lowest foot to the shared ground line, and move the character layer across the static environment.
Close a full gait by interpolating from its last pose back to its first; never reverse one step as a substitute for the opposite-leg step.
